solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Newspaper feature in support of statuary?

blocks.note: first meaning: a regular article by a named writer
second meaning: a pillar, such as one bearing a statue on top

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as playful: a pillar is literally in support of a statue, as Nelson's is.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a regular press article and an upright pillar that holds up a structure or monument.

clue.text: Copper not common in poison

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
something not common is scarce

explanation.surface: A police officer, the 'copper', is unusually involved in a poisoning case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a police officer but gives the metal's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a plant-derived paralysing toxin once used on South American arrow tips.

clue.text: Socialist Worker sales campaign? Car from abroad appears?

definitions.note: a car built abroad for right-side roads appears in this form

blocks.note: socialists are on the political left
a hand is a labourer, as in farmhand
a drive is an organised push, as in a sales drive

explanation.surface: Socialist Worker is a British left-wing newspaper, here apparently running a push to sell copies.
explanation.walkthrough: Socialist Worker looks like the paper's name but splits into two words. Britain drives on the left, so foreign cars there usually have the steering wheel on the left, the opposite of local cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehicles made for countries driving on the right have steering on the left, so an imported car typically shows that layout.

clue.text: Bloke picked up claim to find a lot of correspondence

indicators.note: picking up a sound means hearing it, so the word is taken by how it is said rather than spelt

blocks.note: a bloke is a man, a male, which sounds like the post
to bag something is to claim it for yourself

explanation.surface: A man is collected so he can claim a heap of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mailbag is a sack of letters, so it stands for a large quantity of post.

clue.text: Region in South Africa — or region of ancient Greece

indicators.note: in places the region word inside the two-letter country abbreviation

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for South Africa
a region is a part of a country

explanation.surface: A quiz question offers a choice between a modern African area and a classical Greek one.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'or' suggests two definitions, but only the second is one; the first half is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a city-state and its surrounding territory in the southern Peloponnese of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Item from Biblical book son held in part of hand

indicators.note: something held in a grip sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the palm is the inner surface of the hand
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy holds a scriptural text in his hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the 150 sacred songs in the Book of Psalms is a single item of that Biblical book.

clue.text: Title for bishop, just left-wing, never confused internally

indicators.note: a confused word is muddled, so its letters come out in a jumbled order
internally means on the inside, so the jumbled letters sit within the other word

blocks.note: just and right both mean fair or proper
red is the colour of the political left
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A bishop's honorific is judged fair and leftish, never a muddle on the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left-wing' reads as describing the bishop but gives the colour of the left.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglican bishops are formally styled 'the Right Reverend' before their names.

clue.text: Claim a strand of hair twisted up

indicators.note: in a down answer going up means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a tress is a lock or strand of hair

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a lock of hair has been twisted into an updo.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something is to state it firmly as true, which is what claiming does.

clue.text: Flashy military pilots getting suspicious cut

indicators.note: cutting a word short trims off its final letter

blocks.note: the Royal Air Force, Britain's air arm
something fishy seems suspicious

explanation.surface: Showy air force pilots are given a dodgy haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a haircut but tells you to drop the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffish describes a flashy, slightly disreputable style, as of a rakish charmer.

clue.text: Sign of life and courage on patrol

blocks.note: to have heart is to have courage
a police officer's beat is the area they patrol

explanation.surface: A soldier on patrol shows life and bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse from the heart is the basic evidence that someone is alive.

clue.text: Protection US soldier provided in the main, after retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
in puts one piece inside the other one here

blocks.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea
GI is slang for an American soldier

explanation.surface: American troops offer cover at sea after a withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the sea, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: Aegis means shelter or sponsorship, originally the shield of Zeus, so it is a kind of protection.

clue.text: That fellow in pub backed treatment for alcoholism?

indicators.note: in places the fellow inside the drinking place
backed means moved backwards, so the whole combination is read from end to start

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
the pronoun for a male person

explanation.surface: A man is found in a pub supporting a cure for drinking, an ironic picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is short for rehabilitation, the residential treatment given to people with alcohol or drug dependency.

clue.text: Current measuring device encountered in more than half of America

indicators.note: more than half of a word means keeping its opening letters, just over half of them
in puts the meeting word inside the trimmed country name

blocks.note: the first four of America's seven letters
to have encountered someone is to have met them

explanation.surface: An electrical meter is found across most of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: An ammeter measures electric current in amperes, its name contracted from ampere-meter.

clue.text: Right name, possibly, for traumatic experience

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting the correct name could prevent a distressing ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is literally a bad dream and figuratively any deeply distressing, harrowing episode.

clue.text: Computer program modified real clothing

indicators.note: a modified word has been changed, so its letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: app is short for application, a piece of software
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: Software has altered genuine garments, perhaps a virtual try-on app.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for garments, what people wear.

clue.text: Out-of-date about book and unlikely to change?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps round the second

blocks.note: stale things are past their best
B is the standard abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: An old book seems fixed and unlikely to be revised.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is steady and settled, so it is not expected to alter.

clue.text: Married? Agree to lose initial spirit

indicators.note: losing the initial means dropping the first letter of the word

blocks.note: M is the standard abbreviation for married
to settle a matter is to agree on it

explanation.surface: A newlywed agrees to give up their early enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle means courage and resilience, the sense of 'spirit' as in fighting spirit.

clue.text: Stick seen behind a little creature in stream?

indicators.note: being behind another piece means coming after it in an across answer

blocks.note: a tad means a small amount
a pole is a long stick

explanation.surface: A stick is spotted behind a small animal in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a verb but is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is a frog's larva, a small creature living in streams and ponds; the question mark notes ponds suit it as well.

clue.text: Liver and kidneys, say, not available, entirely running short

indicators.note: running short means falling a letter shy, so the last one is dropped

blocks.note: a dish that is off is no longer available on the menu
entirely means all of it

explanation.surface: A restaurant has completely run out of liver and kidneys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' is the British menu sense: a dish that is off has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the edible internal organs of an animal, of which liver and kidneys are examples.

clue.text: Item of music, quiet, on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: peace is quiet, calm

explanation.surface: A calm instrumental track is being broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a single musical composition, an item in a programme.

clue.text: Cheese — French, originally — in legal case

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: French cheese turns up as evidence in a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' seems to describe the cheese, as Brie is French, but it only supplies its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is the set of instructions and papers given to a barrister for a case, and so the case itself.

clue.text: Left-winger taken aback about blokes in distress

indicators.note: taken aback suggests going back, so the word runs in reverse
about means around, so the reversed word wraps the other piece

blocks.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a hard-left activist
blokes are men

explanation.surface: A radical is shocked to find men upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' reads as surprised but signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment means severe suffering, mental or physical, so it is a form of distress.

clue.text: Still likely to be gutted on a regular basis

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: even and still both intensify, as in 'still better' and 'even better'
just the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone is probably going to be devastated again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' is British slang for bitterly disappointed, but here it removes a word's middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenly means uniformly or at steady intervals, as regular spacing would be.

clue.text: Small toboggan circling start of deep mud

indicators.note: start of a word means only its opening letter
circling means going round, so the sled word surrounds the single letter

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
a luge is a small racing sled
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A little sled goes round the edge of a patch of deep mire.
explanation.definitionFit: Sludge is thick, soft, wet mud or a similar viscous mire.
